ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: If the population of Stoneflies stays the same, what will most likely happen to the population of trout?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: This is a food web diagram. The “Leaves & Algae” on the left has arrows pointing to “Mayflies,” “Stoneflies,” and “Caddis Flies.” In the diagram, the box where “Stoneflies” is located has an arrow pointing to “Trout” on the right, indicating that trout feed on stoneflies or depend on stoneflies as a food source. There is also an arrow in the diagram from trout pointing to “Humans.” Reasoning: The question asks what the trout population would most likely do if the stonefly population remains unchanged. According to the food web relationship, stoneflies are a food source for trout; if this food source does not change, and the question does not state that other conditions change, then the trout population would most likely also remain unchanged.
